analysis:
Examined the changed regions of the PR. (1) docs/reference/configuration.md head lines 587-596 add a 'Prompt preparation and admission' table documenting DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE, _MB, _VERIFY, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_TEMPLATE_LOOPS and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_COLD_LOAD_RELEASE. This is documentation only, but it describes a new provider-side prompt token cache. It reuses rendered chat-template piece token IDs 'in the request's prefix-cache scope' and is turned off by the global DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE disable. (2) provider-swift/Package.swift line 166 adds the 'Hub' product from swift-transformers as a dependency, with the comment 'Tokenizer configurations for the prompt token cache'. The package is already in the dependency graph (the Transformers product is already imported), so this adds no new external package, only another product from an existing one.

No concrete regression is visible in the supplied evidence. The implementation (PromptTokenCache.swift, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites.swift, ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift) is not supplied, so I cannot verify the following. Open questions for integration: (a) whether the new in-memory token-piece cache is keyed by the coordinator-authored cacheSalt scope, so it adds no cross-account timing or sharing channel beyond the accepted SEC-035 / T-041 posture. The doc says 'already seen in the request's prefix-cache scope', and that needs source confirmation. (b) Whether the cache holds only token IDs of prompt text in provider memory, with no persistence to disk. That matters for T-041 and A-001, because the SSD tier's leak #2 stays closed only if nothing prompt-derived is written to disk. (c) Whether DARKBLOOM_TTFT_COLD_LOAD_RELEASE lets later coordinator events overtake a pending model load without weakening T-053 grant/revocation ordering, and whether it has any availability effect (T-010). (d) Whether the Hub product has any network-fetch behavior that tokenizer loading could trigger outside the model-artifact verification path (T-012 / T-027). All of these are unverified contracts, not evidence of a regression.
